purpose: Remove only the standard-LARE discrete hydrostatic residual at the current moving geometry, while retaining the original conservative moving-volume equation and allowing non-equilibrium dynamics to determine the flux response.

rationale.B1_finding: The path-preserving equilibrium control strongly reduces WT_HOLD drift but over-forces moving histories because it adds the flux required to follow the instantaneous hydrostatic storage manifold.
rationale.B2_question: Can hydrostatic discretization drift be removed without imposing quasi-static equilibrium tracking during rapid H(t) motion?
rationale.literature_context: Conceptually aligned with hydrostatic-equilibrium subtraction in Zeng & Decker (2009), but implemented here only as a LARE diagnostic control.

corrected_flux_control.interpretation: At fixed H an exact hydrostatic layer-average state is stationary. When H moves, only the conservative geometry term and state departure drive the trajectory; the control does not force instantaneous hydrostatic equilibrium.

manufactured_checks.fixed_H_equilibrium: For Hdot=0 and state=W_E(H), every corrected flux and every storage derivative must be zero to <=1e-10 cm/day.
manufactured_checks.moving_path_not_a_target: No requirement is imposed that W_E[H(t)] be followed when Hdot!=0.

governed_metrics_all_histories: max absolute total unsaturated storage error

hard_requirements: fine route qualified for all four histories
adjudication.relative_support_rule: B2 receives relative support only if it is component-wise noninferior to B0 on all governed metrics and strictly improves at least one governed metric.
